rv.q: The resulting production proves that the young company also has serious dramatic chops, drawing out the humanity of Kushner’s characters even when the text is dominated by fierce polemical debates.
Blank Theatre Company's revival of Tony Kushner's A Bright Room Called Day is an important one as we head into the bleak times ahead.
Blank Theatre Company’s stirring production proves to be an especially important work for today.
Director Danny Kapinos does a masterful job of merging past and present and his talented cast brings the story of artists facing exile with daring and humor.
As much as I enjoyed their performances, I found myself a little confused over some of the details of the story.

cn.t: Kushner's early, wordy examination of Weimar Republic's fall receives a well-acted, spare production that feels prescient and important, though the play itself proves more intellectually valuable than dramatically satisfying.
